newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE warns it may reconsider role in Albania.
newsitem.headline: OSCE warns it may reconsider role in Albania.

text.p: The political head of Europe's top security forum warned Albania on Friday the body may have to reconsider its assistance to the troubled Balkan nation if political parties cannot agree to hold elections next month.

Foreign Minister Niels Helveg Petersen of Denmark, current chairman-in-office of the 54-nation Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), backed a message by OSCE envoy Franz Vranitzky that Albanian politicians had to establish the basis for elections to be held by the end of June.

"Failure to achieve agreement on such a basis, he indicated, could lead the OSCE and others to reconsider their commitment to assist Albania in overcoming the country's present crisis," Petersen said in a statement issued by OSCE headquarters in Vienna.

"I fully support Dr Vranitzky's position. I therefore call upon the Albanian political parties, and President (Sali) Berisha in particular, to reach agreement as a matter of urgency on the terms of an election law," Petersen added.
He said the parties also had to establish a climate in which preparations for free and fair elections could be properly conducted.

The former Austrian chancellor late on Thursday appeared to have brokered a fresh deal to get the elections back on track after a draft electoral passed by parliament, dominated by Berisha's Democrats, failed to satisfy opposition parties.
The parties said the law favoured the Democratic Party and warn they could boycott the planned election.
